pr.title: Check python3 only when the installer creates a venv
pr.head: 03c988433068aba0ca15a0a451e19ffc8f106a3c

summary: install.sh is Projector's public installer, and project upgrade runs it again to update the CLI. When pipx is missing, the installer gives the CLI a virtual environment (venv) of its own and installs into it with pip. A venv keeps running on the Python that created it, so an upgrade of an existing venv never uses the python3 on PATH.

Before this change the installer still required PROJECTOR_PYTHON, which defaults to python3, to be 3.11 or newer on every run. So an upgrade from a shell whose python3 was older, such as one with an old venv activated or a version-manager override, stopped with exit 69 although the install was healthy. The message also hid the cause: it discarded the interpreter's stderr and never said which Python answered.

The installer now checks PROJECTOR_PYTHON only when it has to create the venv. A venv that already exists but is too old still fails, because pyproject.toml declares requires-python = ">=3.11" and pip refuses the install. A refusal now adds a second line with the version and path that answered, or the interpreter's own error.

groups.title: The installer checks Python only to create a venv
groups.kicker: Where the version check runs, and what its refusal says
intro: install_venv is the installer's path when pipx is not on PATH. It creates the venv when $VENV_DIR/bin/python is missing, installs the CLI into it with pip, and links project into the bin directory.

The version check moves inside the branch that creates the venv, into a new function, require_python. That function runs a short Python script that prints the interpreter's version and path and exits non-zero below 3.11. It captures both output streams, so a refusal can show either the version that answered or the error from an interpreter that could not run.

files.note: Moves the Python version check into the venv-creation branch and adds require_python, which reports what answered.

checks.text: An existing venv now skips the check. In a sandbox, an existing Python 3.12 venv upgraded with PROJECTOR_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3 (3.9), and with no python3 on PATH, exits 0 at this head and 69 on main. A venv made by Python 3.9 still fails at both, with pip's requires a different Python.

The refusal still exits 69 under set -e: the failing substitution sits left of &&, so the function reaches its messages. Checked with an old Python, a missing path, and no python3 on PATH; each prints the second reports: line and creates no venv.

groups.title: Tests run the installer's real check
groups.kicker: A fake interpreter that runs the real script under a chosen version
intro: The installer tests use a fake python3 that logs its arguments and makes a fake venv. Before this change its -c branch simply exited 0 or 1. Now it runs the installer's real check script with the real Python, after setting sys.version and sys.version_info to the version the test chooses, so the tests exercise the real comparison and the real message.

Three tests cover the change: an old Python is refused with the version it reported, an interpreter that cannot run shows its error, and an upgrade of an existing venv runs only the venv's pip under an old python3.

checks.text: The three new tests fail against main's install.sh: this one with 0 != 69, the other two because the reports: line is missing. All 53 installer tests pass at this head.
